In 'Blank Page' (Chapter: 'Blank Page'), what is the central teaching on practice?

In this section of *Blank Page*, the teaching focuses on direct observation of the mind: *"Probably most of us have had some situations in life where we have come to the conclusion, ‘Well, I got what I wanted, but was it really worth it?’ or ‘I didn’t realize it was going to be like this.’ Or ‘I thought this was going to make me happier."* The central guidance is to step back from the habitual impulse to control or fix present experience, and instead cultivate a spacious, non-reactive presence. When we investigate thoughts and feelings without identification (*anattā*), their grip on the heart naturally dissolves. It is like It is like a small boat floating on a calm mountain lake beneath an open sky. Rest in that clear, unentangled knowing.

In 'Blank Page' (Blank Page), how should a meditator handle restless thoughts and mental chatter?

The text reflects: *"Even when we are working with our minds in the meditation hall, thinking, ‘I am going to get jhāna."* Thoughts are merely passing mental formations (*saṅkhāra*); they have no solid core unless we feed them with belief. When a thought arises, simply recognize it as 'thinking, thinking' without jumping into the storyline. It is like It is like a deep ocean holding waves on its surface while remaining utterly still below. Be the vast, open sky through which thoughts pass like harmless clouds.

Observe that tension is an impermanent, conditioned phenomenon arising in awareness. It is like It is like letting muddy water in a glass sit undisturbed until it becomes crystal clear. Allow the knot of tension to unwind naturally in spacious presence.

What is the essence of letting go (vossagga) taught in 'Blank Page' (Blank Page)?

The teaching observes: *"There is a letting go if I-ness, a letting go of having and being, and a letting go of doing."* True letting go is not an act of aggressive rejection, but the wisdom of non-clinging (*anupādāna*). When the mind recognizes that nothing in the conditioned world can provide permanent security, the gripping reflex naturally relaxes. It is like It is like opening the window shutters of a stuffy room to let the fresh mountain breeze flow in. Rest in the relief of an unburdened heart.
